doc.title: Dave Bailey and John McNeil Interview, 1959-10-25

title: Willie Jones (Kaiser), McNeil's teacher, killed by a car
summary: Willie Jones taught McNeil and died in a hit-and-run during a visit from California.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Willie Jones was one of the great, great Clannett brothers. I don't know if you knew him. I know his brother. I know John. John, yeah. John, I played with John. Well I played with John too. Yeah, but I'm talking about the one that John's playing. I'm trying to get him in this outfit that I'm getting together now on the bass. Well I take a few lessons from his brother Willie. Yeah, he's good. And he was a real good drunk man. Well voiced on music. Yeah, read music. Read real good.
Clannett, he played Clannett in sax. That's Kaiser.
That's the one that got killed by the car. They call him Kaiser.
Yeah, yeah. That's what they call him? Yeah, they used to call him Kaiser. Nickman.
He used to come home and teach me music when I was, you know, starting in the field.

He was good man. He was going to make up a band, take me here when he got killed. He had been in California since 1927. Come back here and was only here a month to see people that caught up on him on the static. Right there in the front.
In 47 he went to California. In 47. Yeah. About 27. Did I say 27? No, I said he went away in 1927. No, not 27 because he taught me music in the 30s.
Well then 27 he was with Louis DuBois. Yeah. Well, what was it? I can remember that.
He went to California during the war, right? In the fall.

Well anyhow, he was in California. Come back here to visit the people. They're only here a month. And this car hit him about 2 o'clock on a Saturday evening. Hit him at 4th Street and carried him all the way to the club. And didn't stop. Never stopped. Didn't catch that guy until about one or two weeks after that. Hit him. Hit him. Hit him. Hit him. Hit him. Run drive. And the fellow told me about it. I live on Chippewa Street upstairs. A fellow named Joe Williams. He said, oh David, come to the window quick. What up? He got me excited. What's the matter? He said, you know Willie Joe got killed? I said, no. No. He got killed for Saturday. Calls for a hit him. Hit him. Run drive. And the time he called me I was sick. I was back home.
